alignments.note: Genitive absolute participle with its supplied subordinator *When* (rule 86) and the reflexive the English idiom requires; discontinuous under rule 15.
Expressed subject of the genitive absolute.
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό rendered by the single word *together*, which answers to neither token separately (rule 45); rule 106 assigns the word to this phrase rather than to the compound verb's preverb.
A noncompositional unit never absorbs an intervening article (rule 93).
Impersonal copula with its expletive subject; the supplied *possible* completes what ἔστιν was going to say and is a rule 7 helper on it, discontinuous around the negative under rule 15.
Infinitival *to* is a rule 7 helper on the verb.
Both adjective and noun are anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun under rule 58, discontinuous under rule 15.
Attributive adjective takes the bare possessive-form word.

review_notes: Folding *possible* onto the infinitive rather than onto ἔστιν remains defensible; the ellipsis is in the impersonal copula, which is why it is placed there.
